blocks.text: 1. Embedding Drift

blocks.alt: Embedding quality quietly degrades over time

blocks.text: Embedding Drift closes out the Embeddings module by tying every earlier idea into why embedding quality can degrade over time even without changes.
It closes the Embeddings module by tying every earlier idea into one ongoing maintenance concern.
2. A Quality That Quietly Shifts
As with continuous evaluation over time in Embedding Evaluation, a pipeline that worked well at launch is not guaranteed to keep working well forever.
This topic names and explains that gradual, often invisible decline.
3. Content Drift Versus Model Drift

blocks.alt: Content drift, where data changes, is compared against model drift, where the model changes

blocks.text: The underlying document collection can drift as new content arrives, and the model itself can also be swapped or updated.
These are two distinct sources of the same underlying symptom.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Drift source","What changes"],"rows":[["Content drift","The document collection itself evolves over time"],["Model drift","The embedding model gets swapped or updated"]]}

blocks.text: 4. New Vocabulary Outpacing The Model

blocks.alt: New terms and slang are not represented well by the model

blocks.text: As with why general models fall short in Embedding Fine-Tuning, new terminology, products, or topics can appear faster than a static model was ever trained to understand.
Those new terms get embedded poorly, since the model never learned their meaning.
5. Query Patterns Change Too

blocks.alt: Old query patterns are compared against new query patterns

blocks.text: How users phrase their questions can shift gradually over time too.
An embedding model tuned for yesterday's queries may fit today's less well.

blocks.title: warn
blocks.content: A model fine tuned on last year's support tickets can start underperforming as customers begin asking about new features or using different phrasing than the training data ever captured.

blocks.text: 6. Detecting Drift Through Monitoring

blocks.alt: Retrieval quality metrics are monitored over time to produce a drift alert

blocks.text: As with embedding evaluation, covered earlier in this module, re-running evaluation on a regular schedule reveals a slow quality decline.
Tracking that score over time turns an invisible problem into a visible trend line.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: A retrieval quality score tracked monthly that slowly slides from ninety percent down toward seventy percent over a year provides clear, actionable evidence of drift, long before user complaints alone would have surfaced the same problem.

blocks.text: 7. Responses To Drift

blocks.alt: Drift detected leads to re-embedding content or upgrading the model

blocks.text: As with embedding fine tuning covered in Embedding Fine-Tuning, re-fine tuning on fresher data can restore lost alignment.
Re-embedding the entire collection with a newer model is the more drastic, complete fix.
8. The Re-Embedding Cost
As with switching models cost in Embedding Models, a full re-embed touches every single chunk in the collection.
That cost needs to be weighed against the severity of the drift actually observed.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Drift severity","Reasonable response"],"rows":[["Mild, gradual decline","Monitor closely, consider lighter fine tuning"],["Severe, sustained decline","A full re-embed with an updated model may be justified"]]}

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Embedding Drift Deserves Active Monitoring

blocks.alt: A rapidly changing domain points toward actively monitoring embedding drift

blocks.text: Fast changing domains and evolving user bases need active drift monitoring.
Stable, slowly changing content can rely on far less frequent, lighter monitoring.
10. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates tracking an evaluation score across several months to detect a gradual quality decline.

code.content:
monthly_evaluation_scores = [
    {"month": "January", "precision": 0.91},
    {"month": "April", "precision": 0.86},
    {"month": "July", "precision": 0.79},
    {"month": "October", "precision": 0.71},
]

def detect_drift(scores, threshold_drop=0.10):
    # flags drift once the drop from baseline crosses the threshold
    baseline = scores[0]["precision"]
    for entry in scores[1:]:
        drop = baseline - entry["precision"]
        if drop >= threshold_drop:
            print(f"  Drift detected by {entry['month']}: dropped {drop:.2f} from baseline {baseline:.2f}")
            return entry
    return None

print("Monthly evaluation scores:")
for entry in monthly_evaluation_scores:
    print(f"  {entry['month']}: precision={entry['precision']}")

print("\nChecking for drift:")
drift_point = detect_drift(monthly_evaluation_scores)
if drift_point:
    print(f"\nRecommended action: investigate content or query changes around {drift_point['month']}")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows precision sliding steadily downward month over month, crossing the drift threshold by October, well before the decline would have become obvious informally.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Assuming a well performing embedding pipeline at launch will stay well performing indefinitely.
Never re-running evaluation after initial launch, missing a gradual quality decline entirely.
Confusing content drift with model drift, applying the wrong fix to the actual root cause.
Committing to a full re-embed for a mild decline that a lighter fine tuning pass could have addressed.

blocks.text: 12. Embeddings: Module Complete

items: What are Embeddings introduced converting text into fixed length, meaningful vectors.
Dense Embeddings covered packing meaning into mostly nonzero, compact vectors.
Sparse Embeddings covered huge, mostly zero vectors built for exact term matching.
Hybrid Embeddings covered combining dense and sparse search for the best of both.
Sentence Embeddings applied these ideas at the sentence level.
Embedding Models covered the real, deployed models used to produce these vectors in practice.
Embedding Dimensions covered what a vector's length actually represents and controls.
Similarity Metrics, Cosine Similarity, Dot Product, and Euclidean Distance covered how vectors get compared.
Embedding Fine-Tuning covered adapting a pretrained model to a specific domain.
Embedding Evaluation covered systematically measuring embedding quality.
Embedding Drift closed the module by covering why that quality can degrade over time.
Next up: Vector Databases, covering how these embeddings actually get stored and searched at scale.
